task.title: storypole verify should default to running the gate, with --manual as the explicit opt-out

acceptance_criteria: EVIDENCE 2026-11-06. 'storypole verify GB-243' returned in under 24 seconds with 'verifier: manual
exit_code: Some(0)' and ran nothing; the configured gate was only reached with --run
which is a flag an operator must remember. For a command whose entire purpose is certification
the safe default is the one that executes

and skipping execution should require saying so. Proposed: verify runs the configured command by default; --manual records a human attestation and its receipt says so plainly (it already labels 'manual'

which is honest but currently the default). Pairs with GB-269 (fallback visibility) and GB-268 (config population) - all three concern the same invariant: a receipt must never be stronger than the evidence behind it.
DONE 2026-11-06 (storypole 06936fb)

on the quality-first ruling that a receipt saying exit_code 0 must mean something ran.

Behaviour: 'storypole verify <KEY>' now executes the configured command. --manual records a human attestation instead and its receipt says so; --run is still accepted as a no-op for compatibility. BREAKING CHANGE recorded in the commit footer.

Supporting fix found while testing: unscoped tasks - no crate
no repo
normal for harness-level work - never called verification_command_for at all
so a reserved 'default' entry was unreachable. Now the resolution chain ends with a non-matching probe that lands on 'default'

and root config carries one: 'miter contracts && outfeed lockfiles && chalkline docs check --workspace'.\n\nVERIFIED end to end: 'storypole verify GB-266' with no flags produced verifier: storypole-verify
exit_code: 0 - the suite chain ran. Tier 2: fmt clean
clippy -D warnings clean
55/55.\n\nConsequence to expect: verification now takes as long as the repo's gate (fmt + clippy + nextest + docs
minutes on a cold cache) instead of returning instantly. That cost is the point - two defects today were found only because something finally ran.
